rules.refusal: {code: 'archive_invalid', rule, offset?, member?, typeflag?}; offset is the byte offset of the header block concerned (or of the terminator, or of the first non-zero trailing byte); member is the path once it has been read
reader_order: a zero block: the next block must also be zero (else terminator_missing), then every later byte must be zero (else trailing_data); done
header_checksum: the checksum field is octal digits from its first byte, then only NUL or space; it must equal the sum of the 512 header bytes with the checksum field read as 8 spaces
size_encoding: the size field is octal digits from its first byte, then only NUL or space (no base-256)
path = prefix + '/' + name when prefix is non-empty, else name (each field up to its first NUL); path_invalid, then path_too_long
path_duplicate, then path_collision (equal under ASCII lower-casing)
truncated: the member's data runs past the end of the archive
rules.path_rules: also applied to every files[].path in ck.json (manifest_invalid) and by the packer: components of [A-Za-z0-9._-], no empty, '.' or '..' component (path_invalid); at most 255 bytes (path_too_long); storable as a ustar name of at most 100 bytes, optionally after a prefix of at most 155 bytes ending at a '/' (path_not_ustar)

writer.header: 512 bytes, zero-filled, then: name (offset 0, 100 bytes) and prefix (345, 155) from the ustar split; mode (100) '0000644\0'; uid (108) and gid (116) '0000000\0'; size (124) 11 octal digits then NUL; mtime (136) '00000000000\0'; typeflag (156) '0'; magic (257) 'ustar\0'; version (263) '00'; checksum (148) 6 octal digits, NUL, space, computed with the checksum field read as 8 spaces
writer.split: a path of at most 100 bytes goes in name; a longer one splits at the first '/' that leaves at most 100 bytes after it and at most 155 before it
writer.data: member bytes, then zero padding to a 512-byte boundary
writer.end: two 512-byte zero blocks and nothing after
